problem:
$$
f(t,z)=⟨3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,\text{_____},\,z⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $2{x}^{2}-9{y}^{2}=18$ for $x\ge 3.$ What is the second component of $f?$

feedback.problem:
$$
f(t,y)=⟨\text{_____},\,y,\,4\operatorname{tan}⁡t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,y)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{16}=1$ for $x\ge 1.$ What is the first component of $f?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the hyperbola ${x}^{2}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{16}=1$ for $x\ge 1$ in $xz$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,z⟩=⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,4\operatorname{tan}⁡t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{16} & =(\operatorname{sec}⁡t)^{2}-\frac{(4\operatorname{tan}⁡t)^{2}}{16} \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡t-\frac{16{tan}^{2}⁡t}{16} \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡t-{tan}^{2}⁡t \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t,y) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t,y,\,4\operatorname{tan}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $\operatorname{sec}⁡t.$
